newsitem.title: USA: Intel ups buyback program to 140 million shares.
newsitem.headline: Intel ups buyback program to 140 million shares.

text.p: Intel Corp. said Thursday it will increase its common stock repurchases by up to 30 million shares, bringing its current stock buyback plan to 140 million shares.
Intel's stock jumped $3 to $143.625 early on Nasdaq, where it was the second most-active issue.
With the share increase, 39.9 million shares remain available for repurchase under the authorisation, Intel said.
Under the stock repurchase programme, started in 1990, the computer chip company has repurchased and retired about 92.6 million of its shares at a cost of $4.6 billion.
Intel said its previously announced two-for-one stock split is subject to stockholder approval of an increase in total authorised shares of common stock from 1.4 billion shares to 4.5 billion.
Intel stockholders will vote on the increase at the company's annual meeting scheduled for May 21.
Following the stock split, the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company said the total repurchase authorisation would be 280 million shares.
